text: For the leader. A maskil of the Korahites. [1]
I As the deer longs for streams of water, [AA]so my soul longs for you, O God.
My soul thirsts for God, the living God.When can I enter and see the face of God? [2] [AB]
My tears have been my bread day and night, [AC]as they ask me every day, "Where is your God?" [AD]

Those times I recallas I pour out my soul, [AE]When I would cross over to the shrine of the Mighty One, [3]to the house of God,Amid loud cries of thanksgiving,with the multitude keeping festival. [AF]
Why are you downcast, my soul;why do you groan within me?Wait for God, for I shall again praise him,my savior and my God.
II My soul is downcast within me;therefore I remember youFrom the land of the Jordan [4] and Hermon,from Mount Mizar, [AG]
t[5]Deep calls to deepin the roar of your torrents,and all your waves and breakerssweep over me. [AH]
By day may the Lord send his mercy,and by night may his righteousness be with me!I will pray [6] to the God of my life,
I will say to God, my rock:"Why do you forget me? [AI]Why must I go about mourningwith the enemy oppressing me?"
It shatters my bones, when my adversaries reproach me,when they say to me every day: "Where is your God?"
Why are you downcast, my soul,why do you groan within me?Wait for God, for I shall again praise him,my savior and my God.
